papers.what_it_is: Organizer's 5-page Phase 1 submission guidelines for the 2026 Global Quantum + AI Challenge.

assertions.value: The guidelines list the Phase 1 submission deadline as 15 Sep 2026, review 16 Sep to 14 Nov 2026, finalist notification and Phase 2 start mid-Nov 2026, as guidance subject to change.
quotes: Guidance, subject to change. Milestone Application window opens Phase 1 submission deadline Review and shortlisting Finalist notification Phase 2 PoC Sprint begins
Date April 2026 (at public launch) 15 Sep 2026 16 Sep – 14 Nov 2026 Mid-Nov 2026 Mid-Nov 2026
assertions.certainty_reason: Primary organizer document; table text is flattened by extraction so row alignment is inferred from order.

assertions.value: The concept proposal is limited to 6 pages in PDF with at least 10pt font, plus up to 3 appendix pages, English only, and files of at most 20 MB.
quotes: Concept proposal: maximum 6 pages (A4 or US Letter), PDF format, minimum 10pt font.
Appendices: maximum 3 additional pages. • All text must be in English. • File size must not exceed 20 MB.
assertions.certainty_reason: Direct statement of a requirement in the organizer's own guidelines.

assertions.value: A team may enter several problem statements but must file a separate submission for each, one proposal per problem statement.
quotes: You may submit one proposal per problem statement. A team may submit to multiple problem statements, but each must be a separate submission.
assertions.certainty_reason: Direct rule in the organizer's guidelines.

assertions.value: Submissions are scored against separately published Assessment Criteria, and the guidelines name a clear validation plan with measurable outcomes as one of the strongest differentiators.
quotes: Scored Review: Each submission is evaluated against the Assessment Criteria (published separately).
Define success: a clear validation plan with measurable outcomes is one of the strongest differentiators.
assertions.certainty_reason: The criteria themselves are not in this document; the differentiator line is advice, not a scoring rule.

papers.what_it_is: The team's own Phase 1 HSBC-track submission repository with preregistered gates and a results memo.

assertions.value: The team's headline result is a null: CVQBoost on Dirac-3 trails a tuned gradient-boosted classical detector on the ULB benchmark, and no quantum advantage is claimed.
quotes: The headline result is a null, and it is reported as one.
A quantum-inspired training step (CVQBoost on QCi's Dirac-3) trails a tuned gradient-boosted classical detector on the ULB benchmark.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' own statement; the numbers are in the memo and are measured on hardware.

assertions.value: On hardware, CVQBoost trails the matched-13 tuned GBDT baselines by 0.035 to 0.040 AUPRC, exceeding the minimum detectable effect, and trails on 9 of 10 seeds.
assertions.anchor: RESULTS_MEMO.md gate table and What the evidence says
quotes: abs(delta) > MDE 0.0268; trails on 9 of 10 seeds (only seed 48 positive, +0.0108)
on hardware, by 0.035 to 0.040 against all three tuned GBDTs, every CI excluding zero, 9 of 10 seeds negative.
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured by the authors under a preregistered protocol on one dataset (ULB); not independently replicated.

assertions.value: Gate G0 (tuned XGBoost full-feature AUPRC at least 0.85) failed as committed at 0.8296.
quotes: G0 missed its 0.85 AUPRC floor at 0.8296, and that is reported as a failure
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' measured result on 10 seeds; the memo attributes the floor to an uncorroborated literature band.

assertions.value: Dirac-3 weights closely match an exact classical proxy on the identical Hamiltonian (cosine 0.975 to 0.999, objective 0.013% to 0.413% above the exact minimum).
quotes: weight cosine 0.975-0.999; hardware objective always above (worse than) the exact minimum by 0.013% to 0.413%
assertions.certainty_reason: Measured by the authors on one convex formulation; not independently replicated.

assertions.value: The authors report that neither quantum arm (kernel, tensor network) produced a usable result, and claim no quantum advantage of any kind.

No quantum advantage of any kind.
